The test image shows a soybean stem split lengthwise with **white/cream pith** and darkened/rotted root tissue. Key features:
- Stem interior: white pith (not brown)
- Root zone: dark, decayed tissue
- Lower stem/root area appears severely rotted

This strongly suggests **Sudden Death Syndrome** (white pith is the distinguishing feature vs Brown Stem Rot which has brown pith). Let me verify with reference images.

The SDS reference image (bottom-left panel) shows severely rotted roots and dark lower stem — closely matching the test image. The white pith in the test image is the key diagnostic feature distinguishing SDS from Brown Stem Rot.
